subject.title: Feature: Postcondition checks for cron jobs (deterministic verification of agent outcomes)

question: Should cron post-run verification be implemented as a bounded scheduler-owned verifier, a plugin-owned fail-capable post-run hook, or deferred until a broader agent verification API exists?
rationale: The requested shell verifier crosses command execution, session context, retry semantics, persisted state, public protocol, and plugin/core ownership boundaries, so automation should not choose the permanent contract alone.

options.title: Design bounded scheduler verifier
options.body: Add a typed cron postcondition contract with constrained execution, durable state, retry/escalation behavior, and UI/CLI/docs coverage.

options.title: Add plugin fail hook first
options.body: Expose a supported post-run hook that can fail a cron run and request scheduler-owned retry or escalation while keeping verifier implementation outside core.

options.title: Defer to broader verification API
options.body: Keep this issue open but block implementation until maintainers define a shared verification model for cron, outbound messages, and agent-run claims.

recommendation.title: Design bounded scheduler verifier
recommendation.body: Add a typed cron postcondition contract with constrained execution, durable state, retry/escalation behavior, and UI/CLI/docs coverage.
